place.zh: 沉鼎山 · 后山崖顶 · 草屋
place.en: Mount Chending · The cliff top · a thatched hut

setup.zh: 崖顶一间草屋，屋前青石上一只香炉，三根香已经点上了。瞿老摸出一张红纸：拜师帖，只空着一个名字。
setup.en: A thatched hut on the cliff top; on a blue stone before it, an incense burner with three sticks already lit. Elder Qu takes out a sheet of red paper: a letter of discipleship, one name left blank.

recap.zh: 后山崖顶的草屋前，你在瞿老的拜师帖上写下了名字，送了一根萝卜作束脩，磕了三个头。他三十年没收过徒弟。
recap.en: Before the grass hut on the cliff you wrote your name on Elder Qu's letter of discipleship, gave a radish for the tutor's gift, and bowed three times. He had taken no disciple in thirty years.

zh: 崖顶一间草屋。三根香，已经点上了。
一张红纸，空着一个名字。
「我三十年没收徒弟了。你写不写，自己定。」
en: A thatched hut on the cliff top. Three sticks of incense, already lit.
A sheet of red paper with one name left blank.
"I haven't taken a student in thirty years. Write or don't — your choice."

text.zh: 红纸上的字一笔到底，像扫帚扫出来的；只空着写名字的那一处。
text.en: The characters on the red paper run each in one stroke, as if swept with a broom. Only the place for a name is blank.

text.zh: 三根香已烧下去小半截——他点香的时候，你还在山门挑水。
text.en: The three sticks have burned a good way down: he lit them while you were still carrying water at the gate.

text.zh: 屋檐下挂着一把旧扫帚，比山门那把还秃。
text.en: An old broom hangs under the eaves, balder even than the one at the gate.

story.zh:
到了一处小满从没来过的崖顶。崖顶上一间草屋，屋门半掩着，小满从门缝里瞧进去，里头一张竹床，一张木桌，桌上两只茶杯，一只杯口朝上，杯底还剩着半口冷茶；另一只杯口朝下扣着，扣得端端正正，落了厚厚一层灰，像是很多年没人翻过来了。屋门口一块青石，青石扫得干干净净，一片落叶也没有。青石上一只香炉，炉里插着三根香，已经点上了，倒像是早就知道他会来。

小满走到青石跟前，脚下一顿，把脚抬起来，在旁边的石头上刮了刮鞋底，刮干净了，才踏上去。

瞿老看着他刮鞋底，道：「九月初九那天，在台阶上，你也刮过。」

小满一怔：「……师……老人家看见了？」

瞿老道：「三千多个孩子从我扫的那一级上踩过去。刮了鞋底再踩的，两个。」

小满问：「还有一个是谁？」

瞿老没有答。他在青石边上坐下来，道：「外门弟子，没有师父。你知道为什么？」

小满试探道：「……外门穷？」

瞿老道：「法不传六耳。一个师父，一辈子只教得好几个人。外门几百人，教不过来，只好一起听大课。」他看着小满，「想要师父，得有人要你。」

小满问：「那……有人要我吗？」

瞿老没有回答。他从怀里摸出一张红纸，放在青石上。那是一张拜师帖，帖上的字已经写好了，工工整整，只空着一个名字。他道：「我三十年没收徒弟了。你写不写，自己定。」
story.en:
They came to a cliff top Xiaoman had never been to. On it stood a grass hut, the door half open; through the gap Xiaoman saw a bamboo bed and a wooden table, and on the table two cups — one mouth up, half a mouthful of cold tea still in it; the other turned mouth down, set squarely, under a thick layer of dust, as if no one had turned it over in many years. Before the door lay a bluestone slab, swept clean, not one fallen leaf on it. On the stone a censer, three sticks of incense already lit, as if it had long been known he would come.

Xiaoman came to the bluestone, stopped, lifted a foot and scraped his sole on the rock beside it, and only when it was clean did he step on.

Elder Qu, watching him scrape his sole, said: "The ninth day of the ninth month, on the steps, you scraped them then too."

Xiaoman stared. "…Ma— sir, you saw?"

"Three thousand-some children have trodden over the step I sweep. The ones who scraped their soles first: two."

"Who was the other?"

Elder Qu didn't answer. He sat down at the edge of the bluestone. "Outer disciples have no master. Do you know why?"

Xiaoman ventured: "…The outer court's poor?"

"The Law isn't passed to six ears. A master can teach only a few well in a lifetime. The outer court has hundreds — too many to teach, so they all hear the great lectures together." He looked at Xiaoman. "Want a master, someone has to want you."

"Then… does someone want me?"

Elder Qu didn't answer. He took a sheet of red paper from his coat and laid it on the bluestone. It was a letter of discipleship, the words already written, neat and square, only the name left blank. He said: "I've taken no disciple in thirty years. Whether you write or not, you decide."

label.en: Write your name, and bow three times

exits.means: signs the letter of discipleship and bows

what.zh: 瞿老三十年没收徒弟。他收了你。
what.en: Elder Qu had taken no student in thirty years. He took you.

story.zh:
小满盯着那张红纸看了很久。他想起三试那天，瞿老在第三百级台阶上看他的那一眼；想起入门那天满殿哄笑，只有瞿老说了四个字，腿稳，心细；想起马小宝的滑竿从瞿老身边抬过去的时候，那不偏不倚的一扫帚。他又想起那只玉盒子，想起瞿老看那只玉盒子的眼神。

他拿起笔，在空着的地方写上了自己的名字——沈小满，三个字，写得比哪一回都端正。

写完了，他忽然想起一件事，脸上一红，道：「……师父，我听讲堂上说，拜师要送礼。」

瞿老道：「谁说的？」

小满道：「周师兄说的。他说孔夫子收学生，也要收十条干肉。」

瞿老道：「那叫束脩。」他看着远处的泗水，慢慢地道：「《论语》里有一句，『自行束脩以上，吾未嘗無誨焉』。孔夫子是说：只要你自己拿着十条干肉来，诚心来学，我没有不教的。十条干肉，值不了几个钱，穷人家也拿得出。他要的不是肉，是你自己走过来的那一趟。」

小满道：「那……我走过来了。可我没有肉。」

瞿老道：「嗯。」

小满在身上摸了半天，从袖子里摸出一样东西来，是一根萝卜。这萝卜是他今天早上从伙房里讨来喂小狰的，还没来得及喂。他双手捧着那根萝卜，递到瞿老跟前，道：「师父，我只有这个。」

瞿老看着那根萝卜，看了一会儿，接了过来，在衣襟上擦了擦，咬了一口。嚼了很久，道：「……甜。」

瞿老把萝卜搁在青石上，站起身来，从香炉里拔出三根香，又从怀里摸出三根新的，就着旧香的火点着了，插进炉里。他对着崖外的方向——那边云雾底下是泗水，泗水边上是沉鼎观的正殿，正殿里供着开山祖师——站直了身子，道：「沉鼎观第十一代弟子瞿某，今收徒一人，徐州蒙山沈氏，名小满。上告祖师。」

他说得很慢，一个字一个字的，像是在念一张很旧的单子。念完了，他没有马上坐下，就那么站着，望着崖外的云，隔了好一会儿，才低低地道：「……三十年前，在这块石头跟前，也说过一回。」

小满没听清，问道：「师父说什么？」

瞿老道：「没什么。跪下。」

小满便跪下来，冲着那只香炉三拜九叩，又冲着祖师的方向，端端正正地磕了三个头。瞿老道：「起来。」他没有笑，可是他那只扫了五十年台阶的手，在小满肩膀上按了一下，按得很重。

小满站起来的时候，胸口那只玉盒子硌了他一下。瞿老看了一眼他鼓起来的衣襟，道：「那颗丹。」

小满道：「是。」

瞿老道：「打算什么时候吃？」

小满道：「练到九层圆满。」

瞿老沉默了一会儿，道：「……吃之前，先来问我。」

小满应了一声。他觉得瞿老这句话说得有点怪，可又说不上是哪里怪。

瞿老把一卷薄薄的书扔给他：「内功，《黄庭经》。『上有黄庭下关元，后有幽阙前命门』——上下前后，身中四处要紧的所在。你在讲堂里听过丹田，这四处，这回自己去找。筑基以后才用得上，先背熟了。」

小满道：「是。」他捧着书，低头看了看自己，伸出一根指头，先在脑门上戳了戳，又在肚脐底下戳了戳，又绕到背后去够腰眼，够了半天够不着，身子扭得像一根麻花。

瞿老看着他扭，道：「你做什么？」

小满道：「找那四处。」

瞿老道：「拿指头找，找一辈子也找不着。」

小满道：「那拿什么找？」

瞿老道：「拿气。」顿了一顿，「先背熟了。」
story.en:
Xiaoman stared at the red paper a long time. He thought of the day of the three trials, the look Elder Qu gave him on the three-hundredth step; of the day he entered the sect, the whole hall laughing and only Elder Qu saying four words — sure-footed, careful-hearted; of Ma Xiaobao's sedan chair carried past Elder Qu, and that neither-left-nor-right sweep of the broom. And he thought of the jade box, and the way Elder Qu had looked at it.

He took up the brush and in the blank space wrote his own name — Shen Xiaoman, three characters, more carefully than ever before.

When he'd written it, something occurred to him and his face went red. "…Master, I heard in the lecture hall that becoming a disciple, you bring a gift."

"Who said so?"

"Brother Zhou. He said even Confucius, taking a student, took ten strips of dried meat."

"That's called *shuxiu*." Elder Qu looked at the Si far off and said slowly: "The *Analects* has a line: 'From one who brings a bundle of dried meat and upward, I have never refused instruction.' Confucius meant: so long as you bring your ten strips yourself and come sincerely to learn, there's none I won't teach. Ten strips of dried meat aren't worth much; a poor household can manage it. It isn't the meat he wanted — it's the walk you made to get there."

"Then… I've walked here. But I haven't any meat."

"Mm," said Elder Qu.

Xiaoman felt all over himself a long while and brought something out of his sleeve: a radish. He'd begged it from the kitchen this morning for Little Zheng and hadn't got round to feeding it. He held the radish out to Elder Qu in both hands. "Master, this is all I have."

Elder Qu looked at the radish a while, took it, wiped it on his front, and bit it. He chewed a long time. "…Sweet."

Elder Qu laid the radish on the bluestone and stood, pulled the three sticks from the censer, took three new ones from his coat, lit them from the old, and planted them in the censer. Facing out beyond the cliff — beneath the clouds there lay the Si, and by the Si the main hall of Chending Temple, where the founder was enshrined — he stood straight and said: "Qu, disciple of the eleventh generation of Chending Temple, this day takes one disciple: Shen of Meng Mountain in Xu Province, named Xiaoman. Reported to the founder."

He spoke very slowly, one word at a time, like reading out a very old list. When he'd finished he didn't sit down at once but stood looking at the clouds beyond the cliff, and after a good while said low: "…Thirty years ago, before this stone, I said it once before too."

Xiaoman didn't catch it. "What did you say, Master?"

"Nothing. Kneel."

So Xiaoman knelt, and kowtowed to the censer three times and nine times, and toward the founder bowed three times, very properly. "Up," said Elder Qu. He didn't smile, but that hand which had swept steps for fifty years pressed down on Xiaoman's shoulder, hard.

As Xiaoman rose, the jade box in his coat dug into him. Elder Qu glanced at the bulge. "That pill."

"Yes."

"When do you mean to take it?"

"When I reach full ninth level."

Elder Qu was silent a while, then said, "…Before you take it, come and ask me first."

Xiaoman agreed. He thought it an odd thing to say, but couldn't say what was odd about it.

Elder Qu tossed him a thin book: "Inner art: the *Yellow Court Classic*. 'Above is the Yellow Court, below the Gate of Origin; behind, the Hidden Gate; in front, the Gate of Life' — above, below, front and back: four vital places in the body. You've heard of the dantian in the lecture hall; these four you'll find for yourself this time. It's no use to you till after Foundation — learn it by heart first."

"Yes," said Xiaoman. Holding the book, he looked down at himself, poked a finger at his forehead, then below his navel, then reached round behind for the small of his back, reaching a long while without getting there, his body twisted like a dough twist.

Elder Qu watched him twist. "What are you doing?"

"Finding those four places."

"Find them with a finger and you'll search all your life."

"Then find them with what?"

"With qi," said Elder Qu. A pause. "Learn it by heart first."
